Surah al-Qamar (Makkan except for verse 45, which is Madinan; its verses number fifty-five)

﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been split.﴾ The Hour (al-Qiyamah) has drawn close. ﴿And the moon has been split﴾ it was cleft into two halves over Abu Qubays and Qay'qi'an, as a sign for him (ﷺ). They asked him for it, and he said, "Bear witness." Related by al-Bukhari and Muslim.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 2:

﴿And if they see a sign﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Quraysh, [a sign] being a miracle for him ﷺ, ﴿they turn away and say﴾, [this is] ﴿continuous magic﴾, strong, from al-mirrah (the strength) meaning power, or lasting.
And they denied (the Prophet ﷺ) and followed their desires in falsehood, and every matter, of good and evil, is settled for its people, in Paradise or in Hellfire.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn by al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti, on surah 54, verse 4:

﴿And there had certainly come to them of the reports [that which contains a deterrent].﴾ The reports of the destruction of the nations that denied their messengers. **مُزْدَجَر** (muzdajar) is an *ism masdar* (verbal noun) or an *ism makan* (noun of place), and the **دال** (dal) is a replacement for the **تاء** (ta') of the **افْتِعال** (ifti'al, the eighth verbal form). **ازْدَجَرْته** (izdajartuhu) and **زَجَرْته** (zajartuhu) both mean: I restrained him with severity, forbade him harshly. **ما** (ma) is either a relative pronoun or a descriptive particle.

Wisdom (hikmah) that is complete: "Wisdom" is a predicate of an omitted subject, or a substitute for "mā" or for "muzdajar." "Balighah" means complete, perfect.

"Fa-mā tughni" means "does it benefit them?" Here "mā" is either a negation or an interrogative of denial (istifhām inkārī). On the second reading, it is a fronted object (maf'ūl muqaddam).

"Al-nudhur" is the plural of "nadhīr," in the sense of "mundhir" (warner), that is, the warnings that threaten them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 6:

﴿So turn away from them﴾ this is the benefit (fa'idah) of what precedes it, and the speech is complete with it. ﴿The Day the Caller calls﴾ the Caller is Israfil, and the one governing "the Day" is "they will come out" understood after it. ﴿To a thing terrible/unfamiliar﴾ read with a damma on the kaf and with its sukun, meaning a thing that is denied (munkar) by the souls, and it is the Reckoning.

﴿Khushshaʿan﴾ means humbled, abased. In another reading it is khushshaʿan with a damma on the kha and a fatha on the shin, with the shin doubled. ﴿Abṣāruhum﴾ is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the subject (of the verb). ﴿Yakhrujūn﴾ means the people will come forth ﴿min al-ajdāth﴾ from the graves. ﴿Ka-annahum jarādun muntashir﴾: as if they were scattered locusts, not knowing where they are going, out of fear and bewilderment. The whole clause is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl) referring to the subject of yakhrujūn.

﴿Hastening﴾ meaning rushing, stretching out their necks ﴿toward the caller﴾. ﴿The disbelievers say﴾ among them, ﴿"This is a difficult day"﴾ hard upon the disbelievers, as in al-Muddaththir: ﴿"It is a difficult day, hard upon the disbelievers"﴾.

﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلهمْ﴾ Before them, that is, before Quraysh, ﴿the people of Noah denied﴾. The feminine verb كَذَّبَتْ (kadhdhabat) is used because the word قَوْم (qawm, "people") is treated in meaning as feminine (ta'nith, grammatical feminine agreement). ﴿So they denied Our servant﴾, meaning Noah, ﴿and said, "Mad," and he was rebuked﴾, meaning they reproached him with abuse and other things.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 54, verse 10:

﴿So he called upon his Lord, "Indeed I﴾ with the fath (opening vowel) of the hamzah in "anni," meaning "bi-anni" (that I)

**Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 11:**

﴿So We opened﴾ with the light and the intensive forms (al-takhfif wa'l-tashdid, i.e. the verb read with and without doubling of the second radical), ﴿the gates of heaven with water pouring forth﴾, poured down in a very violent downpour.

"And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs," gushing forth; "so the waters met" the water of the sky and the water of the earth; "for a matter" a state (ḥāl) "already decreed" decided in eternity (al-azal), which was their destruction by drowning.

﴿And We carried him﴾, i.e., Noah, ﴿upon a vessel of planks and nails﴾, which are what the planks are fastened together with, nails and other such things. Its singular is دِسار (disār), like كِتاب (kitāb).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 14:

﴿It sailed on before Our eyes﴾ in full view of Us, i.e., safeguarded. ﴿As a recompense﴾ is in the accusative, governed by a verb understood, i.e., they were drowned as a victory (intisar) ﴿for him who had been disbelieved﴾, and he is Nuh, peace be upon him. It is also read as kafara with the verb in the active voice, i.e., they were drowned as a punishment for them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 15:

﴿And We have certainly left it as a sign﴾ We left this deed as a sign for whoever takes heed from it, meaning its report spread and remained. ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾ One who takes heed and is admonished by it. Its original form is mudhtakir (مُذْتَكِرٌ): the tā' was replaced by a dāl (the unpointed dāl), and likewise the pointed dhāl (ذ), and it was assimilated into it.

﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ That is, My warning (إنذاري). The interrogative *istifham taqrir* (a question intended to elicit affirmation) is used here. *Kayfa* (كيف, "how") is the predicate of *kāna* (كان), and it is used to ask about the state (of the punishment). The meaning is to bring the addressees to acknowledge that the punishment of God, exalted is He, fell upon those who denied Nuh, in its proper place.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 17:

﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance﴾ We made it easy to memorize and prepared it for taking heed. ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾ One who will be admonished by it and will memorize it. The interrogative here carries the sense of a command, meaning: memorize it and be admonished by it. Of the books of Allah, none is memorized by heart besides it.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 18:

﴿The people of ʿĀd denied﴾ their prophet Hūd, and so they were punished. ﴿So how was My punishment and My warning?﴾ i.e., My warning to them of the punishment before its descent, [and how it] fell into its place. He, may He be exalted, has explained this in the following verse.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 19:

﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a wind, harsh and screaming﴾, i.e., intensely loud in its sound, ﴿on a day of ill omen﴾, i.e., of misfortune, ﴿continuing﴾, i.e., constantly ominous, or intense. And it was the day of Wednesday, the last day of the month.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 20:

﴿Tanzi‘u an-nās﴾ — it uproots them from the holes of the earth in which they had buried themselves, and throws them down on their heads, so that their necks break and the head is separated from the body. ﴿Ka’annahum﴾ — and their condition is as has been mentioned — ﴿a‘jāz﴾ (roots, bases) ﴿nakhlin munqa‘ir﴾ — cut off and fallen on the ground. They were likened to palm trees because of their tallness. It is masculine here and feminine in al-Haqqah (69:7), ﴿nakhlin khāwiyah﴾, in consideration of the verse-endings (fawāṣil) in both places.

﴿Thamud denied the warnings.﴾ "Nudhur" is the plural of "nadhir" in the sense of "mundhir" (one who warns), meaning: with the matters by which their Prophet Salih warned them, if they did not believe in him and follow him.

"They said: Shall we follow a single human being from among ourselves? ﴿أَبَشَرًا﴾ is in the accusative by the rule of ishtighal (the grammatical construction in which a verb is occupied with a pronoun referring to a preceding noun, so that the noun is put in the accusative). ﴿مِنَّا وَاحِدًا﴾: the two words are adjectives (sifatan) of basharan. ﴿نَتَّبِعُهُ﴾ explains the verb that governs it (al-fi'l al-nasib lahu). The interrogative is in the sense of negation, as if to say: how could we follow him, when we are a large group and he is one of us and not an angel? That is, we will not follow him. ﴿إِنَّا إِذًا﴾ meaning: if we follow him ﴿لَفِي ضَلَالٍ﴾, that is, going astray from the right course, ﴿وَسُعُرٍ﴾, that is, madness."

﴿Was the Reminder cast upon him from among us?﴾ With tahqiq (pronouncing both hamzas in full) and tashil (softening the second hamza) of the two hamzas, and inserting an alif between them according to both readings, and omitting it. ﴿The Reminder﴾ means the revelation. ﴿Upon him from among us﴾ means that it was not revealed to him. ﴿Nay, he is a liar﴾ in his claim that what was mentioned had been revealed to him. ﴿Insolent﴾ means arrogant and wanton.
﴿They will know tomorrow﴾ in the Hereafter ﴿who is the liar, the insolent one﴾. He (Salih) was (in fact) the one who was about to be punished for their denial of their prophet Salih.

﴿Indeed, We are sending the she-camel﴾, bringing her out of the Hadba, the rock, as they asked, ﴿as a trial﴾, a test, ﴿for them﴾, to test them. ﴿So watch them﴾, O Salih, meaning wait and see what they do and what will be done to them. ﴿And be patient﴾: the ط (ṭāʾ) is a substitution for the ت (tāʾ) of the iftiʿāl (reflexive verb form, with the infixed tāʾ), meaning, be patient over their harm.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 28:

﴿And inform them that the water is to be divided between them, each share of drink being attended,﴾ (the water being divided) between them and the she-camel: a day for them and a day for her. ﴿Each share of drink﴾ (a portion of the water) ﴿being attended﴾ by the people on their day, and the she-camel on her day. They continued in this arrangement, then they grew weary of it and resolved to kill the she-camel.

﴿Then they called their companion﴾ — Qidar, to kill her — ﴿and he took [the sword] and struck﴾ — he took up the sword — ﴿and hamstrung [her]﴾ — with it he hamstrung the she-camel, i.e., killed her, in agreement with them.

Translation of the passage:

﴿So how was My punishment and My warnings?﴾ My warning them of the punishment before its descent, meaning it befell its proper place. And Allah the Exalted explained it in the following verse.

Qur'anic quotation: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a single blast, and they became like the dry, broken branches of the one who builds an enclosure.﴾

Translation of the commentary: He is the one who makes a pen (ḥaẓīrah) for his sheep from dry trees and thorns, to protect them within it from wolves and beasts of prey. Whatever falls from that and is trampled upon is al-hashīm (the dry debris, crushed brushwood).
﴿The people of Lot denied the warnings﴾ (i.e., the matters that warned them, delivered to them through his tongue).

﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a *ḥāṣib*﴾, meaning a wind that pelted them with *al-ḥaṣbāʾ*, which are small stones, each one smaller than a handful, so they were destroyed. ﴿Except the family of Lūṭ﴾, who were his two daughters along with him. ﴿We saved them at *saḥar*﴾, meaning at one of the pre-dawn times, at dawn, on an unspecified day. If a specific day were intended, it would not take tanwīn (nunation, *ṣarf*), because it would be a definite word (*maʿrifa*) deviated (*maʿdūl*) from *al-saḥar*, since its original use is with the definite article *al-*.

Is the ḥāṣib sent upon the family of Lūṭ or not? There are two opinions. The exception is described according to the first opinion as *muttaṣil* (connected, i.e., the exception is from the same category), and according to the second as *munqaṭiʿ* (disconnected), although it is of the same genus, by way of leniency (*tasammuḥan*).

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 54, verse 35:

﴿Ni'mah﴾ is a verbal noun (maṣdar), meaning "as a favour" (in'āman), ﴿from Us. Thus﴾, that is, like that recompense, ﴿do We reward those who give thanks﴾, for whom We have bestowed favours, and who is a believer, or who believed in Allah and His Messenger and obeyed them both.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 36:

﴿And Lot had certainly warned them﴾ — he (Lot) frightened them — ﴿of Our seizure﴾ — Our taking them with punishment — ﴿but they disputed﴾ — they argued — ﴿about the warnings﴾ — about his warning — and they denied them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 37:

﴿And they had certainly sought to have him (Lot) entertain his guests﴾ — that he should leave them alone with the people who came to him in the form of guests, so that they might commit wickedness with them; and they were angels. ﴿Then We obliterated their eyes﴾ — We blinded them and made them as though there were no slit in them, like the rest of the face, by Jibril striking them with his wing. ﴿So taste﴾ — We said to them: taste ﴿My punishment and warnings﴾ — My warning and My threat, i.e., its fruit and its benefit.
﴿And surely a punishment settled upon them early in the morning﴾: the time of dawn, on a day not specified. ﴿A punishment that settles﴾: lasting and continuous with the punishment of the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 41:

﴿And there certainly came to the family of Pharaoh the warnings﴾ — (i.e., his people along with him) — ﴿the warnings﴾ — the admonitions delivered through the tongues of Musa and Harun — ﴿but they did not believe﴾.
They denied Our signs, all of them, the nine that Moses was given. So We seized them with a seizing of One who is Mighty (ʿazīz), Powerful (muqtadir), i.e., strong, able, whom nothing can overpower.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 43:

﴿Are your disbelievers﴾ O Quraysh ﴿better than those﴾ mentioned, from the people of Noah to Pharaoh? So they were not excused. ﴿Or do you have﴾ O disbelieving Quraysh ﴿an immunity﴾ from the punishment ﴿in the scriptures﴾ (al-zubur), the books? The interrogative in both places carries the meaning of negation, i.e., the matter is not so.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 44:

﴿Am yaqooloona﴾ (Or do they say), i.e., the disbelievers of Quraysh, ﴿nahnu jamee'un﴾ (we are a united host), a gathering, ﴿muntasir﴾ (victorious) over Muhammad (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 45:

﴿Soon will the multitude be put to flight, and they will turn their backs.﴾ When Abu Jahl said on the Day of Badr, "We are a victorious host," this verse was revealed. They were then routed at Badr, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was given victory over them.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 46:

﴿Nay, the Hour is their appointed time﴾ for the punishment, ﴿and the Hour﴾ i.e., its punishment ﴿is more calamitous﴾ greater in affliction ﴿and more bitter﴾ more severe in bitterness than the punishment of the world.

Verse 47: ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error﴾ [meaning] destruction by being killed in this world, ﴿and in blazing fire﴾ [meaning] a fire kindled with intensity (with the doubled letter, i.e., musa"ara, meaning kindled and stoked) in the Hereafter.

The commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 48:

﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces﴾ in the Hereafter, and it will be said to them: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾ (i.e., the striking of Jahannam upon you).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 49:

﴿Indeed, We created everything﴾ — "kulla shay'" (everything) is in the accusative (manṣūb), governed by a verb (fi'l) that is explained by ﴿khalaqnāhu﴾ (We created it). It is also read as "kullu" in the nominative (marfū'), as a subject (mubtada') whose predicate (khabar) is ﴿khalaqnāhu﴾ (We created it). ﴿We created it according to a measure﴾ — "bi-qadar" is a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl) of "kull" (everything), meaning: measured (muqaddaran), i.e., determined in its proper proportion.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 54, verse 50:

﴿And Our command is but one word, like a glance of the eye.﴾ Concerning a thing We wish to bring into existence, [Our command is] a single time, ﴿like a glance of the eye﴾ in speed, and it is [Our] saying: "Be," and it comes to be. ﴿Our command is only [a single word]: when We intend a thing, We say to it, "Be," and it is.﴾

And We have certainly destroyed your likes (ashyā'akum), namely those similar to you in disbelief from the past nations, ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾ (This is an interrogative in meaning of a command, i.e., remember and take warning.)

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 52:

﴿And everything they have done is in the scriptures﴾ — i.e., what the servants did is written down, ﴿in the scriptures﴾ — the records of the guardian angels (al-Hafazah).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 53:

﴿And every small and great [thing]﴾ of the sin or the deed ﴿is inscribed﴾ written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 54, verse 54:

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in gardens﴾ (i.e., orchards) ﴿and rivers﴾. The word "rivers" (nahr) is meant as a collective noun, and it has also been read as nuhur with the nun and the ha' both vowelled with a damma, as a plural, like asad (lion) and usud (lions). The meaning is that they will drink from its rivers water, milk, honey and wine.

fi maq'adi sidq — "in a seat of truth": a true assembly, free of idle talk and sin. The word is used in the generic sense (jins), and it has been read as maqa'id (plural, "seats"). The meaning is that they are in gatherings in the Gardens, safe from idle talk and sinfulness, unlike the gatherings of this world, which rarely remain free of such things. This is parsed as a second predicate (khabar thani) and as an apposition (badal), and it is correct as an apposition of part (badl al-ba'd) and of other kinds.

ʿinda malik — "in the presence of a Sovereign": the form is an intensive (mithal mubalagha), meaning one whose dominion is mighty and vast.

muqtadir — "Omnipotent": capable, nothing can overpower Him. He is Allah, exalted is He. The word ʿinda ("in the presence of") indicates station and nearness to His grace, exalted is He.
